editorial:
If you love superhero movies that do not take themselves seriously, this one is a blast. You follow Wade Wilson, a wisecracking mercenary who gets cancer and agrees to a shady experiment to save his life. The treatment gives him amazing healing powers but leaves him scarred and angry, so he puts on a red suit and becomes Deadpool. From there, you watch him hunt down the man who ruined his life while cracking jokes directly at you through the screen. The whole movie feels like a wild, bloody comedy that never slows down.

Ryan Reynolds is perfect in the lead role, delivering jokes at lightning speed while pulling off some seriously impressive action scenes. The fights are creative and fun, and the movie moves fast without feeling rushed. The downside is that the humor is very crude and violent, so it is not for kids or anyone who dislikes dark comedy. If that sounds like your thing, you should stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for the best picture and sound.
endingExplained: In the final showdown, Deadpool faces Ajax on a wrecked ship. Colossus and Negasonic Teenage Warhead help fight off the bad guys. Deadpool nearly kills Ajax but stops when his girlfriend Vanessa asks him to be a better man. Instead of finishing the job, he lets Colossus handle it, though Ajax still dies. Wade and Vanessa reunite, and she accepts his scarred face. The movie ends with Deadpool breaking the fourth wall again, teasing a sequel and joking about the budget.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves R-rated superhero comedy with lots of action and crude humor.
